issues.detail: The check `^## Previous Cycles(?![\s\S]*^## )` (m) requires that no H2 follow Previous Cycles. The protocol says the moved content 'may keep its own headings', and template.md says it is moved 'unchanged, including their headings'. A correct run may therefore keep `## Acceptance Coverage` and `## Technical Acceptance Criteria` as H2 headings under `## Previous Cycles`. The runtime (withoutPreviousCycles, acceptanceInventory) explicitly treats everything after that heading as history, but this check would fail such a run.
issues.fix: In architect-13/spec.json, checks[assertion 1], delete the contains check with regex `^## Previous Cycles(?![\s\S]*^## )`. The remaining `^## Previous Cycles[\s\S]*AC-005` check already requires the heading and the moved coverage below it. check_ok catches AC-004/AC-005 left above it, and any current AC missing coverage after handoff. Leave whether Previous Cycles is the final section to the judge.

issues.detail: Assertion 0 relies on `^(?!\s*<!--\s*STANDARDS)` without the m flag, so it is anchored at the start of the file. This is correct if the grader compiles the regex with only the given flags. With an implicit m flag it would almost always pass, because any line not starting with a provenance block would match.
issues.fix: Confirm that the grader does not add the m flag by default.

issues.detail: Every commit, including the pre-install code and the lockout merge, is dated 2026-10-04T13:00:00Z, while docs/architecture.md cites lockout cycle login-lockout-20260915T101500Z-3c9e4f21. This is slightly implausible history, but it does not affect what the run tests.

summary: The fixture realizes the case well: AGENTS.md makes docs/architecture.md the evident unmarked canonical design, it holds accurate current design plus previous-cycle coverage, criteria, and a Build Plan, and check passes. One assertion-1 check requires Previous Cycles to be the last H2. That would fail a correct run that keeps the moved sections' own H2 headings, which the protocol and template allow, so it should be removed.
